title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound with artificial intelligence-assisted assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction
summary: In a prospective multicentre study, EchoNous KOSMOS point-of-care ultrasound estimated left-ventricular ejection fraction in 424 participants and was compared with transthoracic echocardiography. Agreement was high (overall ICC 0.904); AUC was 0.98 for abnormal ejection fraction (<50%) and 0.99 for severe dysfunction (<30%). This diagnostic-accuracy study does not show improved patient outcomes.
organization: University of Ottawa Heart Institute; University of Ottawa

evidence.tested: Prospective multicentre comparison of AI-assisted point-of-care estimates with comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography in 424 participants. Overall ICC was 0.904; AUC was 0.98 for LVEF <50% and 0.99 for LVEF <30%.
evidence.unknown: The study reports diagnostic agreement, not whether AI-assisted estimates changed care or improved patient outcomes; transport to settings outside the participating centres is not established.
evidence.ai_role: The KOSMOS device's AI interprets point-of-care ultrasound images for LVEF assessment; in 424 prospective multicentre participants, estimates were compared with comprehensive echocardiography.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
